strengths: The paper addresses a critical issue in audio SSL: the heavy reliance on fragile, non-reproducible fine-tuning for SOTA evaluation, and proposes Convex Gated Probing (CGP) as a robust, frozen alternative.

The layer-wise analysis using CGP is highly insightful, demonstrating clearly how weak decoders force final encoder layers to retain low-level reconstruction details and showing how an expressive ViT decoder shifts semantic information to the final layers.

The proposed Better Audio Transformer (BAT) is systematically built with clear ablations on preprocessing, target selection with gated attention, and decoder design, leading to strong performance across multiple benchmarks.

Excellent contribution to reproducibility, detailing the inconsistencies and undocumented heuristics (like extreme loss-scaling) in previous SOTA implementations and providing a clean, open implementation.
weaknesses: While the individual components of BAT (gating mechanism, local min-max scaling, heavy ViT decoder) are largely adapted from prior work in vision and LLMs, their integration in this context is well-guided and highly effective.

The computational complexity of CGP (which scales with the number of layers, tokens, and the 10k prototypes) is not fully discussed. A brief analysis of training and inference times for CGP compared to standard linear probing would be beneficial.

The fine-tuning results of BAT do not exceed the previously reported (though potentially non-reproducible) SOTA of SSLAM on AS-2M (48.55 vs 50.2), although they consistently outperform the reproduced baselines under standardized conditions.

strengths: The paper addresses a critical and highly relevant methodological issue in audio self-supervised learning (SSL): the heavy reliance on unstable, non-standardized end-to-end fine-tuning to evaluate representations.

The proposed Convex Gated Probing (CGP) successfully bridges the performance gap between frozen-feature probing and fine-tuning by accessing all layers via a learnable soft-gating mechanism and utilizing prototypical representations.

The paper modernizes the Data2Vec 2.0 framework to propose BAT (Better Audio Transformer) with several well-reasoned enhancements, including robust dataset-independent preprocessing, gated attention targets, and an expressive ViT decoder.

Excellent empirical analysis: The authors provide an insightful investigation of the layer-wise latent information, demonstrating how a larger decoder shifts the semantic representation peak from middle layers to the final layer.
The paper prioritizes reproducibility, successfully calling out optimization/scaling inconsistencies in current SOTA methods (EAT, SSLAM) and providing a standardized, fair comparison benchmark.
weaknesses: While highly effective when combined, several components of the proposed methods are adapted from existing literature (e.g., D2V2, prototypical probing, gated attention from LLMs, MAE decoders).

The reported fine-tuning (FT) numbers of prior SOTA on AudioSet-2M (e.g., SSLAM at 50.2) still exceed BAT's FT performance (48.55), although the authors adequately explain that this is likely due to hyperparameter sensitivity and lack of reproducibility of prior SOTA under standardized conditions.

CGP requires optimizing a relatively large number of prototype parameters (e.g., K=10k vectors), which makes the probing step computationally and conceptually more complex than standard linear probing.

strengths: Addresses a critical reproducibility issue in recent audio self-supervised learning (SSL) models (like EAT and SSLAM), demonstrating how legacy codebases and fragile optimization heuristics make prior reported results hard to replicate.

The proposed Convex Gated Probing (CGP) offers a robust and effective way to analyze the representation quality across different layers, closing the gap between frozen features and end-to-end fine-tuning.

Provides insightful analysis on layer-wise latent information distributions (Figure 4), explaining how the decoder capacity directly affects whether semantic features peak in middle layers or final layers.
Provides standardized benchmarking on multiple standard datasets (AudioSet, ESC-50, Speech Commands V2) across multiple evaluation protocols.
weaknesses: The paper fails to outperform the originally reported SOTA fine-tuning performance of prior works (e.g., reported SSLAM reaches 50.2 mAP on AS-2M and 40.9 mAP on AS-20k, whereas BAT achieves 48.55 mAP and 41.32 mAP respectively). Despite the fair criticism of prior reproducibility, the claim of establishing an absolute new SOTA is overstated.

The individual architectural components of BAT (e.g., decibel-scale log-compression, local min-max normalization, larger ViT decoder, and gated attention) are mostly existing techniques combined together, limiting the overall methodological novelty of the model.

The complexity and computational cost of Convex Gated Probing (CGP) are not fully detailed. Learning 10k prototype vectors along with gating parameters can be computationally demanding compared to simpler probing techniques.

All intermediate ablation studies (Tables 2, 3, and 4) are evaluated only via CGP on AS-20k. It is unclear if these architectural changes translate to similar gains under standard fine-tuning or on larger pre-training/downstream datasets.

strengths: The paper addresses a critical issue in audio self-supervised learning (SSL): the heavy reliance on full finetuning, which introduces confounding variables and masks the true representation quality of SSL models.

The proposed Convex Gated Probing (CGP) framework effectively bridges the performance gap between frozen-feature probing and full finetuning by combining layer-wise soft-gating with prototypical mapping.

The authors provide a thorough, systematic upgrade of recent audio transformers (yielding BAT) by modernizing the preprocessing pipeline, integrating gated self-attention, and leveraging a heavier ViT decoder.
The empirical evaluation is highly comprehensive, covering multiple benchmarks (AudioSet, ESC-50, SC-v2, SED, HSN, LibriSpeech) and comparing several established probing techniques.

Excellent commitment to reproducibility. The authors detail their attempts and difficulties in reproducing prior SOTA works (EAT, SSLAM), identify undocumented hyperparameters/heuristics, and provide standardized open-source implementations.
weaknesses: While the system as a whole is highly effective and well-designed, the individual technical components are mostly adapted from existing work (e.g., prototype-based probing from Rauch et al., attention-gating from LLMs, and heavy decoder design from MAE).

CGP requires learning and storing a large number of prototypes (10,000 prototypes add ~23M parameters, as shown in Table 10). While still much cheaper than full finetuning, this added parameter/computational overhead during probing is a noteworthy trade-off that deserves more discussion.

The explanation in Section 5.2 regarding why gated attention prevents representation collapse when using End-of-Block (EOB) targets is somewhat brief; a more rigorous mathematical or empirical analysis of how the sigmoid gate changes the attention map behavior in this context would strengthen the paper.

strengths: Highly rigorous and systematic modernization of the audio SSL pretraining pipeline, successfully resolving reproducibility and optimization issues (such as unstable loss-scaling heuristics) present in previous SOTA frameworks like EAT and SSLAM.

Introduction of Convex Gated Probing (CGP), which successfully closes the performance gap between frozen-feature probing and full end-to-end finetuning, providing a reliable, standardized, and faithful evaluation alternative for SSL representations.

Effective integration of Gated Attention in the audio ViT, which prevents representation collapse when using End-of-Block (EOB) targets, resulting in a cleaner and more coherent forward-pass objective.

Extensive, high-quality empirical evaluations spanning diverse tasks (AudioSet, ESC-50, Speech Commands, Sound Event Detection, BirdSet OOD, and LibriSpeech ASR) and comparisons against several probing methods (LP, PB, VQT, H2T, LCGP).

Exceptional transparency and diagnostic analysis, notably the layer-wise latent information visualization (Figure 4) which visually demonstrates how the improved decoder offloads the reconstruction task to later layers.
weaknesses: CGP introduces a non-trivial amount of parameter and memory overhead compared to simpler probes. As shown in Table 10, the probe uses 10,000 prototypes resulting in 23.49M parameters, which is significantly larger than standard linear probing (0.41M). This trade-off between probe capacity and simplicity should be discussed.

The sensitivity of the prototype count K on smaller datasets (like ESC-50 or Speech Commands) is not extensively ablated. While K=10k works well for AudioSet, it is unclear if smaller datasets benefit from fewer prototypes to prevent potential overfitting.

The introduction of the gating mechanism in the attention module adds parameters (matrix WG) and computations to the backbone during both pretraining and downstream inference, but the paper does not explicitly quantify this minor increase in model size/GFLOPs for the backbone itself.

strengths: Outstanding Rigor and Reproducibility Focus: The authors meticulously investigate prior audio SSL methods (EAT, SSLAM), exposing undocumented heuristics (e.g., the extreme loss-scaling factor) and demonstrating a lack of reproducibility in reported finetuning results. They provide clean, native PyTorch implementations to correct this.

Novel and Effective Probing Method (CGP): Convex Gated Probing (CGP) significantly bridges the gap between frozen probing and full finetuning by leveraging a learnable convex layer-aggregation and prototype-based matching. It serves as a more faithful and robust indicator of representation quality.

Well-Ablated and Principled Architectural Design: Every component of the proposed BAT (Better Audio Transformer) is systematically improved and thoroughly ablated, including the dataset-independent preprocessing pipeline, attention gating (which enables stable End-of-Block targets), and an expressive ViT decoder that successfully shifts semantic representations to the final layers.

Extensive Cross-Dataset Benchmarking: The evaluation covers a diverse suite of downstream tasks, including classification, dense sound event detection, out-of-distribution bird sound classification, and automatic speech recognition (ASR).

Excellent Technical Writing and Visualizations: The manuscript is highly readable, with precise formulations, highly illustrative figures (e.g., the attention maps in Figure 5 and layer-wise latent distributions in Figure 4), and exhaustive details in the appendix.
weaknesses: Small Performance Gap under Finetuning: Under full finetuning on AudioSet (AS-2M), the performance improvement of BAT over reproduced baselines is relatively marginal (~1.0 mAP). However, the paper successfully argues that finetuning performance is a fragile and highly sensitive metric compared to probing.

Computational and Parametric Overhead of Probing: Although CGP is far more efficient than finetuning, using 10,000 prototypes introduces considerable parametric overhead (23.49M parameters for the probe) compared to standard linear probing, which might limit its utility on extremely memory-constrained downstream environments.

Incremental Architectural Novelty: The attention gating mechanism is adapted from recent LLM literature (Qiu et al., 2025). While its application to stabilize masked latent regression (MLR) targets is clever and highly effective, the architectural mechanism itself is not entirely novel.
